match.reason: The closest bank point defines natural hazards in general and sorts them into atmospheric and hydrological types, but it never introduces geomorphic hazards, which are land-based events, so it teaches a broader idea than the new point.

draft.title: What a geomorphic hazard is
card: Geomorphic means to do with the land and its shape. A geomorphic hazard is a natural event in the land that can harm people.
Examples are earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides and tsunamis. Each one involves the ground, rock or sea floor moving or breaking out.
An event becomes a hazard when it can harm people, their homes or their work. A landslide on a mountain where nobody lives is still a natural event, but it threatens no one.
Not every natural event is a geomorphic hazard. A heatwave comes from the weather, not from movement of the land.
draft.remember: A geomorphic hazard is a natural event in the land that can harm people.

a.q: Which of these is a geomorphic hazard?
opts: A landslide that buries a road
A heatwave that lasts a week
A drought that dries up a farm dam
A cyclone that brings strong winds
a.why: A landslide is a natural event in the land, and it can harm people by burying a road. The heatwave is tempting because it is a natural hazard, but it comes from the weather, not from movement of the land.
a.clue: Look for the event where the land itself moves.

b.q: A volcano erupts on a remote island where no one lives. Which statement is the best description of it?
opts: It is a natural event in the land, but it harms no one
It is a geomorphic hazard, because it harms many people
It is not geomorphic, because nobody is living nearby
It is a weather event, because ash rises into the sky
b.why: An eruption is a natural event in the land, so it is geomorphic. With no people nearby it harms no one, so it is not a hazard to anyone. The second option is tempting, but it claims harm that does not happen.
b.clue: Ask two things: is it in the land, and does it threaten people?

a.best: A landslide that buries a road

b.best: It is a natural event in the land, but it harms no one

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'The second option is tempting, but it claims harm that does not happen.' Options are shown in random order, so 'second option' does not reliably point to the right one. In this order it is 'It is not geomorphic, because nobody is living nearby', which claims no harm. The why should name the distractor by its content, the one calling it a geomorphic hazard that harms many people.
